transcript:
This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Rylan Barton.
President Trump announced a $25 million program today to encourage the public to blow the whistle on suspected fraud in the federal government.
If you turn somebody in and you, let's say, report and you find a billion dollars,
we are giving a commission to that person of one percent.
It's a lot of money.
Trump says anyone whose tip leads to a conviction or a federal enforcement action would be eligible for payments of up to $30,000.
Trump said he'll be the arbitrator of who deserves the reward money.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky says early warning systems have resumed after a call with Secretary of State Marco Rubio.
But Rubio says the U.S. never did anything to deliberately harm Ukraine, as NPR's Michelle Kellerman reports.
Rubio calls it outrageous that some in Washington said that people are dying because the U.S. is denying Ukraine information.
That's scandalous. That's outrageous. That's just simply not true. That's not accurate.
He spoke for 45 minutes with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, who says the two talked about sensitive things,
including intelligence, satellite connections, and an ongoing delay in delivering interceptors.
Zelensky then met with President Trump's envoy, Steve Whitcoff, in Oslo and says Ukraine is ready to stop hitting sensitive parts of Russia's energy sector if Russia stops bombing Ukraine's.
Whitcoff heads next to Russia. Michelle Kellerman, NPR News, the State Department.
President Trump says he'll spend more than $400 million on the midterm elections, the vast majority of how much his super PAC MAGA Inc. has.
Some Republican strategists had complained that Trump was late to unleash money.
Meanwhile, billionaire Michael Bloomberg is making a late $80 million investment in Democratic races.
Many food prices continue to be pushed higher by labor and fuel costs, but as NPR's Joe Hernandez reports, some items are getting cheaper.
The price of ground beef has gone up 85 percent in the past decade.
Coffee prices have increased due to severe weather in countries like Brazil and Vietnam, and the cost of a chocolate chip cookie has also risen.
But some grocery prices have fallen recently.
Egg prices dropped this year as farms rebuilt their flocks after a severe avian flu outbreak.
And butter prices are also down in response to an oversupply of milk.
Economists say the price increases happening in grocery stores now are in addition to the major price hikes driven by the COVID pandemic several years ago.
Joe Hernandez, NPR News.
A New Jersey food importer filed a lawsuit today challenging President Trump's use of a depression-era law to levy a 50 percent tariff on $20 billion worth of Canadian goods.
This power has never been used in a trade dispute, let alone tested in court.
The Gellert Global Group, which imports Canadian cheese, filed the suit with the U.S. Court of International Trade.
U.S. stocks rose today. This is NPR News from Washington.
The European Union has unveiled a plan to boost its presence in the Arctic as the region warms four times faster than the global average.
As ice melts, new shipping routes are opening, increasing competition for resources and raising security concerns.
The EU plans to protect undersea cables and establish a maritime security hub to track Russian vessels, among other activities.
Oysters are critical to the health of the Chesapeake Bay, with each adult filtering up to 50 gallons of water a day.
Overharvesting has decimated their ranks, but reporter Ari Daniel met one man working to bring them back.
John Consoli of Eastern Maryland marvels at these mollusks.
I think I'm more enthusiastic about something that's like a rock than anybody else could possibly be.
He started by growing them off his pier.
Oh, this one's heavy. Hold on. That's what I need in my son. Hold on.
But ever since he got hooked, he can't help but spread the good word within his community.
That includes neighbors, his dental hygienist, and a local restaurant.
It teaches me just how something that seems so insignificant can make a difference.
Consoli estimates his networks helped add well over a million oysters back to the Bay.
For NPR News, I'm Ari Daniel.
The NFL says security will be heightened for the game in Paris between the Pittsburgh Steelers and New Orleans Saints on Sunday.
After protests engulfed the French capital last weekend, the NFL says league officials are working closely with Parisian police.
The league says there was never a point that the game was in danger of not being played.
I'm Rylan Barton, and you're listening to NPR News from Washington.

topics.text: President Trump announces $25 million program paying whistleblowers for reporting federal fraud
Zelensky says Ukraine's early warning systems resume after call with Secretary Rubio
Trump pledges over $400 million for midterm elections as Bloomberg makes late Democratic investment
Grocery prices mixed: ground beef and coffee rising, while eggs and butter fall
New Jersey importer sues over Trump's 50 percent tariff on Canadian goods
European Union unveils plan to boost Arctic presence amid warming and shipping routes
Maryland oysterman John Consoli works to restore Chesapeake Bay oyster population
NFL boosts security for Steelers-Saints game in Paris after weekend protests
